text:
Brandt-Ueno Civil won the contract to rebuild the Okarra Bridge, the Inland Transport Authority said Tuesday, beating two rivals in a bid valued at 84.6 million quills. The 410-meter span, damaged in last year’s flood surge, will be replaced with a higher-deck structure designed to carry heavier freight loads and reduce closure risk during monsoon season.

Work is set to begin in early March, with completion targeted for late 2028. The authority said Brandt-Ueno’s proposal included local sourcing for steel and a 14-month faster delivery schedule than the next-best offer.

For the civil works sector, the award points to sustained demand for resilience projects, especially where aging logistics corridors are being upgraded after weather losses.
